transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-29 15:00 PST | Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jonas (Redwood SE), Priya (CSM) | Laura (Maplecrest Head Security), Mark (Dir AI), Nina (Infra), Samir (PM)

Summary (auto): quick run through of security requirements for pilot, align on success criteria and next steps.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for hopping on, can you hear me ok?
[00:05] Laura (Maplecrest): yup, loud and clear. thanks.
[00:10] Maya: cool, i'm maya, ae at redwood, i'll run through goals; jonas is our se who will drive the benchmark and priya from cs will track the pilot.
[00:20] Jonas (Redwood SE): hi all, quick technical intro — we'll need to nail down the security constraints up front so the bench is representative.
[00:30] Mark (Maplecrest): quick note: we're a healthcare org, PHI in scope, so we need SOC2 and ISO, also data residency for the pilot — for now US-only.
[00:40] Nina: and infra wants vpc peering or private deployment — ideally no public internet egress for requests that contain PHI.
[00:50] Maya: understood. want to confirm the pilot scope — 4 week pilot, ingesting historical clinical notes, run NER and summarization workloads, expected 50k tokens/day average with 200k peak on batch runs?
[01:05] Samir: yes that's close. Success criteria: 99th perc latency under 700ms for short prompts (<=256 tokens), cost ~x per 1k tokens target (we'll share exact number offline), and no data exfil issues.
[01:20] Jonas: 700ms 99th for hosted is aggressive but doable with batching and kv cache; for private/dedicated we can tighten it. we'll capture token size distribution during the bench.
[01:35] Laura: about compliance docs — we need SOC2 Type II report, ISO 27001 cert, pen test summary, and a data flow diagram showing where PHI is stored and how keys are handled.
[01:50] Maya: yes we can share our SOC 2 Type II and ISO attestation; pen test summary we can provide redacted findings. we'll also include our data flow diagram and KMS options (customer-managed KMS is supported for private deployments).
[02:05] Mark: KMS — can we bring our own HSM/KMS? for private we have our own key management, for hosted we want CMEK if possible.
[02:15] Jonas: currently we support CMEK via ACM integrations and KMS across supported clouds; for on-prem we can point to HSM integration, but specifics we'll map during the tech deep dive.
[02:30] Nina: audit logs — we need fine-grained access logs, per-user/token usage logs, and immutable audit trail for admin actions for 1 year. retention longer if possible.
[02:45] Priya (CSM): we have an audit export pipeline; retention configurable, and we can export to your SIEM (splunk, sumo, etc.). i'll add export templates to the pack.
[02:55] Laura: also SSO — we use SAML 2.0 with Okta. need SCIM for provisioning and RBAC to map to our internal roles.
[03:05] Maya: ok we support SAML and SCIM; RBAC is role-based with admin/dev/viewer roles but we can add custom roles for pilot. jonas, can you capture specifics?
[03:15] Jonas: yeah, we'll need a test IdP metadata file from you; we can spin up an integration in the sandbox. expected flow: SAML assertion -> map to Redwood role -> token issuance. we'll bring a sample mapping doc.
[03:30] Mark: what's the user session length and token revocation flows? for example if we remove an account in Okta, how quick is access revoked?
[03:40] Jonas: SCIM-based deprovisioning is near real-time for sessions; token TTL is short for interactive sessions and we have revocation hooks. exact numbers in the security pack.
[03:55] Samir: on network controls — you mentioned VPC peering vs private deployment. what's the typical turnaround for a private sandbox?
[04:05] Maya: a private sandbox can be provisioned in 1-2 weeks with network config done, assuming firewall rules and peering set. hosted with VPC peering is faster but depends on customer's network team.
[04:20] Nina: our infosec will want to run an onboarding checklist and maybe an initial vulnerability scan. is that okay?
[04:30] Maya: absolutely — we'll agree to a scannable window and provide contact points.
[04:35] Laura: do you encrypt data at rest and in transit? where are audit logs stored?
[04:40] Jonas: yes TLS 1.2+ in transit, AES-256 at rest; audit logs are write-once in our logging service and can be forwarded to your SIEM. for hosted we store logs in the region of the deployment; retention is configurable.
[04:55] Mark: are there any known gaps for HIPAA covered-PHI? any BAAs?
[05:05] Maya: we do sign BAAs with enterprise customers; for the pilot we can agree to a BAA in principle and start work under a pilot agreement. legal will follow up.
[05:15] Laura: ok. benchmarks — what's your recommended benchmark workload pattern?
[05:20] Jonas: recommend a mix: 60% short prompts (<=256 tokens) for triage/NER, 30% mid (256-1024 tokens) for summarization, 10% long (>1024) for long-form summarization. include prefix caching scenarios. we'll run 3 test days: baseline, burst, and sustained.
[05:40] Samir: for scoring success, besides latency and cost, we want quality thresholds using prompt evals — false positive NER rate < x% (we'll define).
[05:50] Maya: noted, add evals to bench plan.
[05:55] Laura: about data handling — do you cache queries or keep KV cache that might persist PHI? need clarity on what is persisted and for how long.
[06:05] Jonas: KV cache is in-memory for inference nodes; optional persistent cache exists for speed but for PHI workloads we recommend no persistent cache or explicit redaction. we can configure per-route cache TTLs or disable cache entirely.
[06:20] Nina: what about prompt logging — we need redaction of PHI before logs leave the environment. any pre-log hooks?
[06:30] Jonas: yes we support pre-log processors and redaction pipelines; we can run a redaction step in the private deployment or in your VPC. we'll show the sample processor.
[06:45] Mark: ok good. can you share an example audit log entry format?
[06:50] Priya: i'll include sample log entries in the pack — includes timestamp, user_id, route, model, token counts, and decision reason fields.
[06:58] Laura: retention policy — 1 year is mandatory, 3 years preferred. are you ok with exporting to our archive?
[07:05] Maya: yes exports supported. retention configurable, we can ship logs to your S3 with lifecycle policies.
[07:12] Samir: timelines — pilot start target 2026-12-14 if security reviews complete. is that feasible?
[07:18] Maya: yes that's feasible if docs and SAML metadata come in early December.
[07:25] Nina: ok we'll target the 12th; note our security review window is 5 business days once docs received.
[07:30] Laura: any legal paperwork? NDA/BAA?
[07:33] Maya: we'll send an NDA and draft BAA; legal will follow.
[07:40] Mark: about cost — we might start with hosted but reserve option to move to dedicated depending on perf/cost. any guidance?
[07:50] Jonas: for your workload and PHI constraints, dedicated or private gives more control for KMS and network. hosted with CMEK is possible but check egress rules. we'll model costs in the bench report.
[08:05] Samir: technical deep dive — can we schedule a 60-min session next week to go over exact network flows and KMS options?
[08:15] Maya: yes i'll loop in solutions architecture and propose times.
[08:20] Jonas: i'll prepare the benchmark config and sample scripts (load generator, tokenizer configs, sample prompts).
[08:28] Laura: one more thing — we need evidence of background checks for any contractors who will access logs. is that documented?
[08:35] Priya: background check policy summary included in the security pack.
[08:40] Mark: are there any RBAC nuances? for example can we have a role that sees metrics but not the raw prompts?
[08:48] Jonas: yes we support field-level redaction in the UI and APIs; you can create roles that mask prompt text but allow metrics and token counts. we'll include role mapping examples.
[08:58] Samir: what about rate limits and quota enforcement? we need to ensure burst allowed up to a certain limit without dropping requests.
[09:05] Jonas: for pilot we can set burst policies and queueing; if you require hard SLAs we recommend dedicated pools.
[09:15] Laura: any third-party subprocessors? where are logs replicated?
[09:20] Maya: subprocessors list included in the pack; logs stored in region with optional replication. we'll put subprocessors and data flow diagram in the docs.
[09:30] Mark: ok practical next steps recap?
[09:32] Maya: i'll send security pack (SOC2, ISO, pen test summary, data flow, RBAC doc) by 2026-12-03. jonas will schedule bench and technical deep dive for first week of December. nina will provide SAML metadata by 2026-12-06. we'll aim to start pilot week of 2026-12-14.
[09:50] Laura: sounds good. any blockers?
[09:53] Nina: none from infra if we get clear network instructions.
[09:58] Samir: legal OK to receive NDA/BAA drafts.
[10:02] Maya: great. we'll follow up in email and add calendar invites.
[10:10] Jonas: one quick note — for perf bench we need a sample of real tokens distribution; mark can you share sanitized sample dataset?
[10:18] Mark: yes we can provide a sanitized set by 2026-12-04.
[10:22] Maya: perfect, thank you. any final questions?
[10:30] Laura: not right now. thanks everyone.
[10:35] Maya: thanks all, meeting adjourned.
